code_label: Hybrid quantum-classical binary classification pipeline
text_span: we define and benchmark a hybrid quantum-classical machine learning pipeline by performing a binary classification task applied to a real-world financial use case.
rationale: States the paper’s main objective and application context.

code_label: Quantum reservoir layer on neutral atoms
text_span: implement a Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) layer within a classical routine
rationale: Identifies the central methodological design.

code_label: Two encoding schemes tested
text_span: The reservoir layer has been executed on QuEra’s Aquila, a 256-qubit neutral atom simulator, using two different types of encoding: position and local detuning.
rationale: Captures the two encoding choices and platform used.

code_label: Financial default prediction use case
text_span: The developed pipeline is applied to predict credit card defaults using a public dataset and a wide variety of traditional classifiers.
rationale: States the target task and dataset type.

code_label: Noise degrades performance
text_span: noise significantly degrades overall performance.
rationale: Summarizes a key empirical finding about hardware noise.

code_label: Noiseless emulation is competitive
text_span: the noiseless emulation achieves competitive performance with the fully-classical pipeline
rationale: Reports the main comparison outcome for emulation.

code_label: QRC potential despite comparable results
text_span: the flexibility and scalability of QRC highlight strong potential for a wide range of applications.
rationale: Presents the authors’ broader interpretation of the approach.

code_label: NISQ constraints motivate low-depth methods
text_span: NISQ-era platforms are characterized by a limited number of qubits
rationale: Frames the hardware constraints motivating the work.

code_label: Analog simulators may improve NISQ methods
text_span: the emergence of analog quantum simulators bears the promise of more efficient execution of some classes of NISQ methodologies.
rationale: States the motivation for using analog quantum simulators.

code_label: Aquila selected for scale and local detuning
text_span: we decided to target the analog neutral atom quantum simulator Aquila
rationale: Identifies the chosen platform and why it was selected.

code_label: Local detuning is a distinctive capability
text_span: the possibility to apply local detuning to the atom arrays.
rationale: Highlights a platform feature central to the experiments.

code_label: Real-world imbalanced classification problem
text_span: We decided to test the effectiveness of the methodology in the context of an imbalanced classification problem.
rationale: States the problem type and why it was chosen.

code_label: Public dataset chosen for reproducibility
text_span: we opted for a publicly available dataset [8] that has been frequently referenced in prior studies
rationale: Explains the dataset selection criterion.

code_label: Reservoir computing reduces training complexity
text_span: only the output layer is trained, typically a simple classifier with relatively few parameters.
rationale: Describes the reservoir computing principle used to motivate the approach.

code_label: Prior neutral-atom QRC work informed encoding choices
text_span: The latter two showed better performances for the tasks considered and therefore will be implemented and tested in this work
rationale: Explains why position and detuning encodings were selected.

code_label: Pipeline has three stages
text_span: the implemented pipeline is composed of three steps
rationale: Summarizes the overall workflow structure.

code_label: Preprocessing includes cleaning scaling PCA and aggregation
text_span: The dataset is preprocessed using standard methodologies in order to obtain a set of relevant features from a cleaned dataset;
rationale: Captures the preprocessing stage at a high level.

code_label: Classical reservoir benchmark included
text_span: Classical Reservoir Computing (CRC): the whole pipeline remains unchanged, while the quantum reservoir computing layer is replaced by a classically-equivalent counterpart.
rationale: Identifies the classical baseline used for comparison.

code_label: Fully classical baseline included
text_span: the classifiers are applied directly to the features obtained after the preprocessing phase.
rationale: Defines the fully classical comparison pipeline.

code_label: Dataset cleaning removed inconsistent records
text_span: the initial step in our preprocessing is data cleaning, removing negligible samples whose features appear to have undocumented values.
rationale: Describes a key data-cleaning decision.

code_label: Nested smaller datasets for quantum runs
text_span: Due to limited quantum resources, the entire dataset was not executed on Aquila.
rationale: States a resource limitation affecting experimental scale.

code_label: Categorical variables converted to boolean features
text_span: The dataset contains two categorical variables SEX and MARRIAGE that we addressed by converting them into boolean features
rationale: Records a preprocessing transformation.

code_label: PCA retained 11 components
text_span: the selection of 11 principal components, which approximately explain 99% of the total variance in the dataset.
rationale: Captures the dimensionality reduction decision.

code_label: Features aggregated into 12 groups
text_span: we then aggregate the 24 features into 12 groups using hierarchical clustering in the principal component space.
rationale: Describes the feature aggregation step.

code_label: Reservoir increases dimensionality to capture nonlinear dependencies
text_span: The subsequent reservoir computing step then increases the dimensionality of the data with the specific objective of capturing non-linear dependencies among features
rationale: States the intended role of the reservoir layer.

code_label: Position encoding maps features to atom spacing
text_span: the separation between the ith and the (i + 1)th atoms is given by ri,i+1 = r0 + δri →r0(1 + λf i).
rationale: Defines the position-encoding mechanism.

code_label: Detuning encoding maps features to local detuning amplitude
text_span: this strategy directly maps the i-th feature f i to the amplitude of the local detuning drive
rationale: Defines the detuning-encoding mechanism.

code_label: Reservoir outputs are Z and ZZ expectations over time
text_span: the expectation values of Zi and ZiZj operators for each pair of atoms must be computed for a set of timesteps.
rationale: Specifies the observable features extracted from the reservoir.

code_label: Feature dimensionality depends on encoding
text_span: the detuning encoding scheme produces 78 features per time step
rationale: Quantifies the output size for detuning encoding.

code_label: Position encoding yields more features
text_span: In the case of position encoding, one additional qubit is required to represent the features.
rationale: Captures the dimensionality difference for position encoding.

code_label: Short pulse sequence chosen to fit coherence time
text_span: we decided to use 5 timesteps of 0.5 µs each.
rationale: Records the timing choice made to fit hardware constraints.

code_label: Classical reservoir is a dequantized equivalent
text_span: the Classical Reservoir Computing (CRC) benchmark is a dequantized version of the QRC
rationale: Defines the classical reservoir baseline.

code_label: Resampling applied only to training set
text_span: All resampling methods were applied exclusively to the training set to avoid data leakage.
rationale: Important methodological safeguard.

code_label: Oversampling and undersampling methods tested
text_span: we evaluated both oversampling and undersampling techniques
rationale: Summarizes the imbalance-handling strategy.

code_label: F1-score used for tuning due to imbalance
text_span: The selection criterion was the F1-score on the validation set, a metric well-suited for imbalanced classification tasks
rationale: Explains the model-selection metric.

code_label: Accuracy avoided because it can mislead
text_span: accuracy was deliberately avoided because of its tendency to provide misleadingly high values in the presence of class imbalance.
rationale: States a metric-related caveat.

code_label: DNN benchmark architecture
text_span: The model architecture consists of six fully-connected layers with dropout regularization to prevent overfitting.
rationale: Describes the classical deep-learning benchmark.

code_label: Emulation used to set parameters and baseline
text_span: This preliminary phase allowed us to evaluate the performance of our method in a controlled, noiseless environment
rationale: Explains the purpose of the emulation stage.

code_label: Shot count plateau reached at a few hundred evolutions
text_span: The performance seems to reach a plateau when performing a few hundred emulated Hamiltonian evolutions.
rationale: Reports the shot-count sensitivity observation.

code_label: Statevector emulation competitive with DNN
text_span: the resulting F1-score for all considered reservoir models is compatible with the performance achieved by DNN, particularly for statevector emulations.
rationale: Summarizes the emulation benchmark outcome.

code_label: Training time advantage over DNN
text_span: the training time increases when applying oversampling methods and a decreases for the undersampling one.
rationale: Captures the reported training-time trend.

code_label: SVM training time prohibitive
text_span: Concerning SVM, training time is prohibitive with respect to other classifiers
rationale: Highlights a negative performance finding for one classifier.

code_label: Hardware noise lowers performance
text_span: The negative impact of hardware noise on classification performance is consistently observable: emulation results are always better than those obtained using the actual hardware.
rationale: States the main hardware-vs-emulation comparison.

code_label: Detuning generally outperforms position on hardware
text_span: the detuning encoding generally performs better than or at least comparable to the position encoding in all the configurations considered.
rationale: Reports the encoding comparison on Aquila.

code_label: Correlation degrades at later timesteps
text_span: the correlation degrades at later timesteps, likely due to the onset of decoherence effects.
rationale: Identifies a time-dependent degradation pattern and its likely cause.

code_label: More shots beyond 200 give little improvement
text_span: increasing the number of measurements, particularly beyond 200, does not lead to a substantial improvement in statistical correlation.
rationale: Reports the shot-number threshold observation.

code_label: Optimal measurement count selected
text_span: we selected an optimal number of measurement samples nopt = 240, corresponding to 40 shots per timestep and dataset sample.
rationale: Records the chosen experimental setting.

code_label: More samples help classifiers ignore noise
text_span: the classifiers become more capable of recognizing and discarding machine-induced noise when more samples are available.
rationale: Explains why performance improved on the larger smaller dataset.

code_label: Hybrid approach advantageous over pure quantum learning
text_span: This is an encouraging result for the use of QRC, compared to other QML techniques where the learning is performed only through the quantum module.
rationale: Provides the authors’ interpretation of the hybrid design advantage.

code_label: QRC can match complex neural networks
text_span: the combination of QRC and simple classifiers can achieve a performance comparable to more complex neural networks
rationale: Restates the main conclusion about predictive performance.

code_label: Shorter training and fewer resources than DNN
text_span: the considered classifiers require shorter training times and less computational resources than the deep neural network.
rationale: Summarizes the efficiency advantage.

code_label: Register size limits encoding and sampling
text_span: the register size is the main limiting factor for both the amount of input data that can be encoded in an atom array and the achievable sampling rate
rationale: States a platform limitation affecting scalability.

code_label: Future gate-based QRC suggested
text_span: Further research directions may include applying gate-based implementations of QRC to the same dataset
rationale: Explicit future work direction.

code_label: Digital QRC could enable dataset-tailored methods
text_span: The digital version of QRC could allow for methods specifically tailored to the dataset at hand
rationale: Another stated future direction with hedging preserved.
